readerTitle: Five idle vans, one new market: write the plan
caseNote: 가상 시뮬레이션 (가정용 해충 방제 업체가 식당 대상 B2B 정기 서비스를 출시) · 모든 인물과 수치는 설명용
insight: 시장 진출 계획은 서류가 아니라 순서가 있는 판단의 사슬이다. 누구에게 먼저 팔지를 좁게 정해야 메시지, 판매 방식, 출시 후 학습이 모두 그 고객에 맞춰진다.
misconception: 시장 진출 계획은 최대한 넓은 시장을 잡고 광고와 할인으로 빨리 키우는 것이다.

sources.text: 시장 진출(go-to-market)의 표준 개념: 첫 고객 선정, 메시지-시장 적합, 판매 방식, 출시 후 학습
모든 인물, 업체, 수치는 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: 모든 수치는 가상입니다. 6주 후 14곳 계약, 첫 달 이후 4곳 해지(약 29%)라는 설정이 카드 5와 6에서 일치하는지 확인했습니다.
위생 점검 시 해충 방제 기록을 확인하는 관행은 지역마다 다릅니다. 특정 국가의 규정처럼 읽히지 않도록 'a written service log ready for your next inspection'처럼 일반적으로만 썼습니다. 점검관이 기록을 '인정한다'는 표현은 쓰지 않았습니다.

cards.title: Five idle vans, one new market: write the plan
body: Dana runs a pest control company with five vans. Summer is booked solid with homes. Every winter, three vans sit in the lot.
Her idea: monthly service contracts for restaurants, which need pest control all year. You'll make four calls for her, in order. Each one shapes the next.

image.label: Three pest control vans parked in a snowy lot while two drive out
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 눈 덮인 주차장에 같은 디자인의 작업용 밴 세 대가 서 있고, 두 대만 출발하는 모션 라인. 밴에 실제 회사 로고나 상표는 넣지 않음. 겨울의 한산한 분위기.

cards.title: Who do you sell to first?
body: The city has hundreds of restaurants. Dana can make maybe ten sales visits a week on top of running the business.

options.text: Every restaurant in the city, to reach the most prospects
options.feedback: More names on the list, but visits scatter across town, vans waste hours driving, and no owner hears about Dana twice.

options.text: The 60 independent restaurants on routes her vans already drive
options.feedback: Cheap to serve, easy to visit, and owners on the same street talk. A few happy customers become references for the next ones.

options.text: A regional chain with 40 locations, to fill winter in one deal
options.feedback: A big prize, but chains buy slowly through head office and can demand terms a five-van company can't meet yet. One customer would hold all the power.

cards.title: Say you chose the 60 on your routes. What do you say to them?
body: Dana talks to eight owners. None of them say "bugs." They say "a failed health inspection," "a bad review," "a closed kitchen."

options.feedback: It builds some trust, but it's about Dana, not the owner. Nothing says why to act this month.
It invites a price comparison and attracts the owners most likely to leave for the next cheaper offer.

options.text: "Visits before you open, and a written service log ready for your next inspection"
options.feedback: It uses the owners' own worry in their own words. They can picture the inspector's visit going well.

cards.title: Say you chose the inspection message. How do owners hear it?
body: A contract means a stranger in the kitchen every month. Each one is worth a few thousand dollars a year to Dana.

options.text: A booking page plus local online ads
options.feedback: Cheap and always open, but letting someone into your kitchen is a trust decision. Few owners will sign a yearly contract from an ad.

options.text: Dana visits in the 3 p.m. lull and offers a free 15-minute kitchen check
options.feedback: The deal is big enough to justify her time, and owners see the problem with their own eyes. The check does the selling.

options.text: Flyers on every restaurant door on her routes
options.feedback: Low cost, low effort, and low trust. Busy owners throw out flyers with the menus from other suppliers.

cards.softwareNote: Software founders face the same call: a self-serve sign-up page fits small, low-risk purchases, while a product that touches sensitive data or costs thousands a year usually needs a person in the sale.

cards.title: Say you chose the visits. Six weeks later, 14 signed and 4 cancelled.
body: Winter vans are busier. But four restaurants left after their first month, and Dana doesn't know why.

options.text: Expand to the whole city now, while there's momentum
options.feedback: You'd copy an unknown leak into a market ten times bigger, and lose customers faster than you can visit new ones.

options.text: Call the four who left and four who stayed before expanding
options.feedback: Say the calls reveal the paper log kept getting lost, and owners wanted a photo report by text. A cheap fix, found before it spread.

options.text: Offer the four a 25% discount to come back
options.feedback: It may win back some revenue, but it treats a problem you haven't diagnosed and teaches customers that leaving earns a discount.

cards.callout: After the fix, Dana expands one neighborhood at a time, using each street's customers as references for the next.

cards.title: Dana's go-to-market plan fits on one page.
body: Notice that each line only makes sense because of the line above it.

breakdown.label: First customers
breakdown.detail: 60 independent restaurants on existing van routes

breakdown.label: Message
breakdown.detail: Pre-opening visits and a log ready for inspection

breakdown.label: Channel
breakdown.detail: In-person visits with a free kitchen check

breakdown.label: After launch
breakdown.detail: Talk to leavers and stayers before expanding

cards.softwareNote: A software launch plan uses the same four lines: which users first, which words match their pain, self-serve or sales-led, and what churn or usage tells you before you scale.

cards.title: A plan is a chain of guesses.
body: Every line rests on the first one. If Dana had picked the wrong first customers, the message, channel and fixes would all be tuned to the wrong people, and the plan would look fine on paper.
The plan also expires. When Dana moves on to hotels or hospitals, buyers, worries and buying processes change. Rewrite every line, starting with who, instead of copying what worked for restaurants.

cards.title: Go to market one decision at a time, in order.
body: Each call you made maps to an idea in this unit:
list: **Who first:** a narrow group you can reach cheaply
**Message-market fit:** their worry, in their words
**Sales-led vs self-serve:** match the channel to the size and trust of the deal
**Learning after launch:** find the leak before you scale
**Launch sequencing:** expand street by street, using references
cards.callout: **Try it today:** write your own one-page plan with four lines: who, what you say, how they hear it, what you'll watch. Circle the line you're least sure of.
